doc.title: Clyde Kerr Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006

chapter: The future of New Orleans music
title: Avant-garde and the Improvisational Arts Quintet with Kidd Jordan
summary: New Orleans has not embraced avant-garde players; his quintet with Kidd Jordan and Alvin Fielder plays without charts, and tradition means moving forward.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: You know I think the average person when they think of New Orleans music they probably typecast it into well yes, I know Dixieland jazz came from there and maybe a little of the Neville Brothers. I don’t know, I count myself in this category, that I didn’t realize how much — different kinds of things were actually coming out of New Orleans.

Right. And even now as we try to rebuild and regroup, there’s been a part of New Orleans music and New Orleans culture for instance that has not been embraced and mainly it’s the really avante garde sorry to say. I don’t like the word but that’s the type of musician Kidd Jordan is. The kind of musician I am too because I can do that as well as play, because it’s all the same thing. But unless you sound something like Louis Armstrong or whatever like that man, it’s like it doesn’t matter. Whatever you do it doesn’t matter. With the Improvisational Arts Quintet, that’s the group I play with Kidd and Alvin Fielder, we get on the bandstand and sometimes we may not see each other for a year or so and we just get together and start playing. In the beginning of that group we used to play charts and stuff, well not charts but heads of tunes. After you play the head then you’re off on your own. But now we don’t play that no more, we will just show up

and react among ourselves. And to me that’s the whole essence of improvisation. There’s no chords, no particular form, you just make it up as you go. And when you can come together and have those moments like that more, you can’t beat that you know. But New Orleans hasn’t embraced that. To me I think New Orleans is confused or they can’t look at the real thing about playing traditional music, creating music or creating music and the tradition that it was created. What I mean by that, if Louis Armstrong wouldn’t have taken the initiative to take it further from the guys who he was listening to we would never know about him. So traditional music is playing the way it was or the way, in the beginning, playing in the tradition is to take something that’s been done already and bringing it forward.
